note: Written by the Product Feed agent each morning. This first edition was hand-picked from real articles as a sample.

articles.title: Advanced evals: How to find (and fix) hidden AI failures in your product
articles.author: Hamel Husain and Shreya Shankar
articles.summary: Start with error discovery: find the failures that matter to your product before choosing metrics. Their example is Harvey, which rebuilt its AI contract reviewer this way and nearly doubled its internal quality score.
articles.why: A method you can apply to your own product before you write a single PRD.

articles.title: Product managers need a new operating system for the AI era
articles.author: Nayan Teja
articles.summary: When information is abundant, alignment becomes the constraint. AI takes over low-leverage PM work, which makes the quality of product judgment far more visible.
articles.why: Useful framing for how your agent team should report to you.

articles.title: AI in product management: what's (really) changing?
articles.summary: The main constraint on teams is moving from engineering output to product judgment, AI product strategy and decision quality.
articles.why: Maps onto where you want to grow: judgment over output.

articles.title: Evals are the new PRD
articles.summary: PRDs assume you can fully specify a system's behaviour up front. AI products can't be specified that way, so measurable signals that verify the behaviour you want take the PRD's place.
articles.why: Directly shapes how your PM agent writes specs for Projects.

articles.title: AI evals for product managers: a beginner's guide
articles.summary: Dashboards can't see inside an agent. The guide walks through traces, LLM judges, offline and online evals, and how to tie them back to product outcomes.
articles.why: A gentle on-ramp if the Lenny piece feels dense.

articles.title: Product management in the age of AI: from roadmaps to reasoning systems
articles.author: Victoria Clotet
articles.summary: LLMs, autonomous agents and probabilistic systems in production are changing both the technology stack and what a product manager is responsible for.
articles.why: A broad overview to anchor the rest of this week's reading.

articles.title: Stop shipping AI features. Start shipping the evals first.
articles.summary: An argument for building the evaluation before the feature, with pointers to the practitioners and methodology documents worth reading next.
articles.why: Short, opinionated, and good for a Frameshift angle.

articles.title: The AI adoption curve in product teams
articles.summary: A survey of what PMs actually want AI to do, led by insight synthesis and analysis, and why strategic gains still lag: AI can inform decisions but can't make them.
articles.why: Real practitioner data for your own content and decisions.

articles.title: How AI changes product management in 2026
articles.summary: An AI model without clear outcomes, steering metrics, user value and safety checks is a liability. The bar is to be a PM who is good because of AI.
articles.why: A checklist you can hold your own agents to.

articles.title: The new AI growth playbook for 2026: how Lovable hit $200M ARR in one year
articles.author: Elena Verna
articles.summary: A long conversation with Lovable's head of growth on how growth works for AI-native products.
articles.why: Directly relevant to the road to $10K MRR.
